newsitem.title: CHINA: Fire kills eight, injures dozens in China hotel.
newsitem.headline: Fire kills eight, injures dozens in China hotel.

text.p: A fire that raged through a hotel in central China has killed eight people and seriously injured 31, some of whom leapt from upper-floor windows to escape, police said on Thursday.

The manager of a privately contracted restaurant on the second floor of the Yanshan Hotel in Changsha, capital of central Hunan province, had been detained after he turned himself in and two other managers had been arrested, local police said.
All eight deaths from the fire that swept through the hotel in the early hours of Wednesday were due to smoke inhalation, an official of the Public Security Bureau in Changsha said by telephone.
An earlier report by the official Xinhua news agency that 30 people had been killed and dozens injured was wrong, he said.

The injured had been taken to nine hospitals in Changsha. Most were suffering from excessive smoke inhalation, although some were hurt when they jumped out of windows on the top floors of the seven-storey hotel to escape, he said.
"I saw the whole thing," the official said. "About 30 people jumped out of the windows on the top floors but none of them were killed because they wrapped themselves in quilts."
Officials in city hospitals earlier said they were treating the injured for smoke inhalation, burns and broken bones.
About 172 guests were staying in the hotel when the fire broke out and officials sent 21 fire engines and more than 800 police and firefighters to the scene, the police official said.

The number of fire disasters in China in 1996 declined by 3.5 percent compared with the previous year to 36,856, Xinhua quoted an official of the Ministry of Public Security as saying on Wednesday. There were a large number of casualties, the official said, but gave no details.

China implemented safety measures in hotels, restaurants and cinemas in 1995, sharply cutting the number of major fires after a string of fire disasters in 1994 killed 2,600 people and injured 4,000, making it China's deadliest year on record.
